decision_conditions: Condition : 1 - 1.	Due to its size, prominent and elevated position and materials, the shed is considered harmful to the appearance of the property, the streetscene and the area as a whole. It is contrary to Unitary Development Plan policies ENV-B.1.1 (New Development) and H.6.4 (Extensions and Alterations). The shed dominates the site and appears to overdevelop it, particularly given its proximity to the dwelling.

Condition : 2 - 
INFORMATIVES

1.	To ensure that pedestrian safety is maintained, it is recommended that a splay of 2.4m X 2.4m be provided on each side of the access, the depth measured from the back of the footway and the widths outwards from the edges of the access, and no fence, wall or other obstruction to visibility exceeding 0.6m in height above the surface of the adjoining highway shall be erected within the areas of such splays. As such it is recommended that the existing brick wall be modified to achieve the above guidelines. 

2  If the shed were to be relocated to a position further away from Camborne Way than the side wall of the original house (excluding any extensions that may have been added since the house was first built) and provided it is used only for purposes incidental to the enjoyments of the house, it would be 'Permitted Development' for which you would not need to obtain planning permission. Please advise the local planning authority within one month if you intend to do this and if so, by when.
description: Erection of a detached shed in rear garden to house.
